subject: Workplace Skills
title: Handling Contradictory Instructions
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Handling Contradictory Instructions.

hook.text: Monday: 'Focus on quality.' Wednesday: 'Ship faster.' Friday: 'Why isn't this both fast and perfect?'

buildup.text: Contradictory instructions often come from bosses under competing pressures they haven't resolved themselves.

discovery.text: Surfacing the contradiction respectfully forces a priority decision. This is a service, not insubordination.

twist.text: Silently choosing which instruction to follow is risky. You might pick the wrong one without realizing it.

climax.text: Say: 'I want to deliver well. Right now I see tension between speed and quality. Which should I prioritize this week?'

punchline.text: Name the tension. Let them resolve it. Then execute.

quiz.question: What should you do when your boss gives contradictory instructions?
options: Follow the most recent instruction and ignore the rest
Respectfully surface the contradiction and ask for prioritization
Do both tasks at a lower quality level
